the design of network communities is a complex process that requires understanding of the social and technical affordances that support their creation.
network communities are a technosociological construct that requires understanding both of the technology and the community that it supports.

network communities can be seen as a genre of collaboration that is robust and persistent, based on a sense that locality spans both the virtual world and the physical world, that requires understanding of technology and sociality, that can be seen in historical antecedents, that has design implications for designers, that is an area of research for researchers, and that is an area for community members to consider.

understanding the social, technical and cultural factors that contribute to the formation and evolution of communities in the network society.
the development of new forms of collaboration and sociality that span both the virtual and the physical worlds.
understanding how network communities can be used to support the social and collaborative needs of people.

network communities are a rich and fertile area of research and design for the CSCW and CHI communities.

network communities are something old, something new, something borrowed and something blue.
